description: LamSuite Billing Statutory GST Test Vectors covering all statutory and commercial edge cases to the paisa. v1.1 adds the CR-C supplier-bill charge stage (TC11-TC20): an optional top-level 'charges'[] input and 'expected_charges'[] output, plus charge totals inside 'expected_totals'. v1.2 adds the CR-C-11 payable policy (TC21-TC22): an optional top-level 'separately_paid_in_payable' flag that decides whether a separately-paid charge is inside what the supplier is owed, with 'in_payable' per charge. TC01-TC10 are sales-side and MUST NOT change.
rounding_convention: Per line, in integer paisa: EXCLUSIVE taxable = discounted base, GST = round_half_up(taxable * gst_percent / 100) and cess = round_half_up(taxable * cess_percent / 100). INCLUSIVE (MRP includes tax) taxable = round_half_up(discounted base / (1 + (gst+cess)/100)) and total tax = discounted base - taxable, so taxable + tax is exactly what the customer is charged. The GST amount is then split cgst = round_half_up(gst/2), sgst = gst - cgst, so the two halves always sum to the line's GST. Rounding each half off the taxable base instead loses a paisa whenever both halves round down. CHARGES (CR-C): a charge is taxed by the same primitives, evaluated after bill-discount allocation and before round-off, split intra/inter-state by the SUPPLIER's place of supply, with the sign of the amount applied to the tax. Add-to-cost charges are spread over the bill's lines in integer paisa: floor the exact quotient per line, then hand the leftover paisa out one at a time to the largest fractional remainder, ties to the first line in grid order, so the allocations always sum exactly to the charge's taxable amount plus any non-creditable tax on it (unrecoverable GST is capitalised with the charge); a basis that sums to zero places the whole amount on the first line in grid order. A charge treated as expense posts amount + non-creditable tax to the expense register and puts only the creditable tax in input tax. A charge marked paid_separately is computed identically but excluded from charge_taxable_total, charge_tax_total, charge_total, total_tax, net_before_round and grand_total; it is reported only in the separate_charge_* totals while still spreading into landed cost and still counted as creditable input tax. taxable_subtotal always stays goods-only, and per line landed_unit_cost equals the charge-inclusive effective_unit_cost (PUR-002). The reconciliation identity asserted by every charge vector: goods taxable + landed_cost_addition + expense_charge_total + creditable_input_tax_total == (grand_total - round_off) + separate_charge_total.
